tip: To avoid duplicate patients, send an ‘If-None-Exist’ header with a unique identifier search query (e.g., If-None-Exist: identifier=system|value). Include ‘Prefer: return=representation’ to get the created resource payload without a separate read.

To prevent duplicate Patients, include a unique identifier element and use the ‘If-None-Exist’ header with a search query (e.g., Patient?identifier=system|value) for a conditional create.
After searchResources, check Bundle.total. If total > 0, take entry[0].resource.id; if total == 0, treat as a new patient but still output a <patient_id> tag (e.g., with a placeholder or 'new').
Inspect the Bundle’s total and entry[]. If total>0 and entry array is non-empty, read entry[0].resource.id. If total==0, branch to classify as a new patient.
After receiving a Bundle, check bundle.total > 0 and bundle.entry; if true, extract entry[0].resource.id and wrap it in <patient_id> tags.

After receiving the Bundle, check bundle.total. If total is 0 (no matching entries), treat as a new patient and output the fallback <patient_id>NEW</patient_id> as specified.

After calling createResource, parse the response body’s “id” field and use that value when reporting the created resource ID.

Before searching, call getSearchParams("Condition") to confirm the correct search parameter codes (e.g., "patient") and their types/targets.

If the patient’s existence is certain, you can omit getResourceById to reduce calls and go straight to searching related resources.
Use the full reference form, e.g. patient=Patient/{id}, to ensure unambiguous matching and add a _count parameter to limit bundle size if many entries are expected.

Avoid making identical repeated search calls. After receiving a Bundle, check Bundle.total and use the Bundle.link with relation='next' to retrieve additional pages instead of reissuing the same request.
Use the Specification’s SearchParameters for 'Condition' to confirm valid parameter codes (e.g., 'subject' or 'patient') before issuing search requests.
Check that the returned Bundle includes a total field and an entry array. If total is 0 or entry is empty, respond with ‘No medical history found.’

When calling createResource for a ServiceRequest, include your full resource body inside a ‘body_json’ property as required by the tool interface, and ensure it contains resourceType, status, intent, subject, code, and occurrenceDateTime.
Use the ServiceRequest.occurrenceDateTime element (e.g. “2025-05-01T00:00:00Z”) to schedule the procedure, matching the FHIR definition for occurrence[x].
Always include a ‘body_json’ field containing the ServiceRequest JSON when calling createResource, e.g. createResource({body_json: {"resourceType":"ServiceRequest", …}}).
Ensure all required elements per StructureDefinition are present: status, intent, subject, code (procedure code), and occurrenceDateTime or occurrencePeriod before invoking createResource.

Include required elements: set status (e.g. "active"), intent (e.g. "plan"), subject.reference to the Patient (e.g. "Patient/PAT002"), code.CodeableConcept to identify the procedure (e.g. text or a code from a procedure value set), and occurrence[x] (e.g. occurrenceTiming.event or occurrenceDateTime) for the scheduled date/time.
Use the ‘subject’ parameter (not patient) to reference the patient, and verify with getSearchParams that ServiceRequest.subject is the correct filter.
Filter by occurrence (occurrence.ge and occurrence.le) to constrain the date window, since ServiceRequest uses occurrence rather than date for planned timing.
Use status=active (or intent=order/plan) to find scheduled requests, as ServiceRequest.status does not include ‘scheduled’.
Use the 'occurrence' parameter with ge/le date range (e.g., occurrence=ge2025-10-27 and occurrence=le2025-11-10) to filter ServiceRequest for planned surgery dates.

OperationOutcome shows 'period' is invalid for CarePlan. Call getSearchParams('CarePlan') to list valid filters (e.g., use 'date' with comparators) or switch to ServiceRequest for scheduling searches.

Avoid unsupported parameters like period; CarePlan supports only date, not period, for time-based searches (e.g., date=ge2025-10-27&date=le2025-11-10).

Filter by subject, category, and occurrence: use params subject=PAT102, category=surgery, occurrence=2025-11-10 to find surgery orders scheduled on the target date.
If searchResources returns a Bundle with total=0, handle the missing Patient (e.g., report or abort) instead of stopping silently before creating downstream resources.
Include the mandatory 'patient' reference (min=1), a 'relationship' CodeableConcept (e.g., code for 'father'), and at least one identifier or name to satisfy minimum cardinality.

If a search returns zero results, surface a clear error or verify the identifier rather than repeating the same search.

Populate mandatory elements: 'status', 'beneficiary' (Patient reference), 'subscriber' or 'policyHolder' (RelatedPerson reference), 'period' (start/end dates), 'payor' (Organization or RelatedPerson), and at least one class with 'type' and 'value' for group and plan identifiers.

Include a unique Identifier on RelatedPerson (e.g. system: http://example.org/relatedperson, value: mother-of-PAT002) and use a conditional-create (If-None-Exist: patient=PAT002&relationship=mother) to avoid duplicate creations.

Populate Coverage.identifier with a business identifier (system|value) and use a conditional-create header (If-None-Exist: identifier=system|value) or upsertResource to enforce idempotent coverage creation.
Use the 'patient' search parameter (alias for beneficiary) in a single searchResources call to retrieve Coverage resources for a given patient instead of issuing duplicate queries.

Inspect Bundle.total and Bundle.entry: if entry list is non-empty, extract the first entry’s resource.id and skip additional calls. You can also include _count=1 in the search to limit results to a single match.

Use the ‘beneficiary’ reference search parameter and check Bundle.total; if total >0, loop through Bundle.entry to extract each Coverage.id and support multiple coverage records.
After creating the RelatedPerson, wrap the returned id in the exact tags requested, e.g., <RELATED_PERSON>{id}</RELATED_PERSON>.
For idempotency, include an If-None-Exist header with a search like 'patient=Patient/{id}&relationship=SPS' to prevent creating duplicate related persons.
Validate the patient reference with a getResourceById('Patient/{id}') call before creating the RelatedPerson to ensure the target Patient exists.
Include an Identifier and use the If-None-Exist header with that identifier to make the createResource call idempotent and avoid duplicate RelatedPerson entries.
If you need the same patient repeatedly, retrieve it once and reuse the result rather than calling getResourceById multiple times.
Before creating a new Account, search with subject=Patient/{id} to see if an Account already exists for that patient and avoid duplicates.
Ensure the required status element is always included (e.g., "status":"active") and supply subject as an array of Reference objects per the resource definition.
Wrap your Account resource object inside a 'body_json' parameter and include required fields such as status (min=1) before calling createResource to avoid input validation errors.
Cache or reuse the retrieved Patient resource instead of calling getResourceById multiple times if no new context is needed.
Use a conditional create (If-None-Exist header) with search criteria like 'subject=Patient/PAT002' (or 'patient=PAT002') to prevent duplicate Account creation.
Cache the fetched Account resource to reuse its state instead of refetching the same resource multiple times.
Cache the fetched RelatedPerson resource when referenced repeatedly, reducing unnecessary reads.
Include the current versionId in an If-Match header on updateResource to enforce optimistic locking and avoid conflicting changes.

Before referencing a RelatedPerson as guarantor, verify its relationship.coding uses the correct system (http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-RoleCode) and code (e.g., FATHER) to capture the intended role.

When searchResources for Account?subject=Patient/PAT001 returns total>0, extract the first entry's resource.id and embed it in <ACCOUNT>resource.id</ACCOUNT> in your response instead of performing another search.
Include the required 'status' element (e.g., 'active') and a 'subject' reference to Patient/PAT001 in the Account createResource body to satisfy the minimum cardinality requirements.
Use the ‘subject’ search parameter with the full reference format ‘Patient/{id}’ to reliably locate an Account for a given patient.
After confirming existence via searchResources, invoke updateResource (even as a no-op) to satisfy downstream workflows expecting a write step following the read.
After using searchResources to find an Account by subject, call getResourceById("Account/{id}") to fetch complete resource details rather than relying solely on bundle entries.
When creating an Account, populate mandatory fields like status (min=1) (e.g., "active") to satisfy required constraints and avoid creation errors.
Use the 'patient' search parameter to filter accounts by patient, e.g., GET /Account?patient=PAT001, to retrieve any accounts linked to the patient.

Use the 'patient' search parameter when querying Account resources (e.g., Account?patient=PAT002) to retrieve accounts associated with the patient.
In the returned Bundle, access entry[].resource.guarantor[].party.reference (e.g., 'RelatedPerson/123') and parse the reference string to extract the guarantor ID.
Use the ‘patient’ search parameter (e.g. Account?patient=PAT002) to find Account resources for a given patient ID rather than unsupported parameters.
After fetching an Account, inspect the Account.guarantor array; each guarantor.party.reference is like “ResourceType/id”. Split on “/” and take the trailing segment as the guarantor’s ID.

After getting the Bundle of Slot entries, parse each entry’s start date-time, sort them in ascending order, and choose the entry with the minimum start value.
Add the _sort=start parameter to your search (e.g., ?status=free&start=gt2025-10-27T20:17:47Z&_sort=start) so the server returns slots in ascending start‐time order. Then pick the first entry’s id.
After fetching all free Slot entries, parse each resource.start (ISO8601) value, sort the entries ascending by this start time, then pick the first entry’s id as the earliest slot.

When you retrieve a Bundle of Slot resources, parse each Slot.start into a date-time object, sort the slots by start ascending, and then pick the first slot in that sorted list to ensure the earliest slot is selected.
Use the ‘communication’ token parameter (e.g., communication=urn:ietf:bcp:47|en) instead of chaining communication.language, which is not supported.
Apply the ‘address-city’ search parameter (e.g., address-city=Boston) to filter practitioners by city on the server side rather than post-filtering client-side.
To fetch the latest slot, sort start times descending with '_sort=-start' and limit to one result via '_count=1'.
Validate parameter codes with the Practitioner SearchParameter list; use 'communication=es' instead of 'communication-code' to filter by language.
When zero practitioners match all criteria, consider relaxing optional filters or return an OperationOutcome indicating no matching practitioners.
Use 'actor=Practitioner/{id}' to locate schedules for a given practitioner before searching for slots.
Query Slot with 'schedule=Schedule/{id}' and 'status=free'; include '_sort=-start' to retrieve the latest available slot first.
Use the valid 'communication' token parameter (not 'communication-language') to filter by language (e.g., ?communication=es).
Use the 'actor' reference parameter with Practitioner/{id} and status=free to find available slots (e.g., ?actor=Practitioner/PROVIDER0002&status=free).

After performing the search, inspect the Bundle.total field. If total is 0, respond exactly with 'No available cardiology slots found.' Otherwise, wrap the numeric total in <SLOT_COUNT>…</SLOT_COUNT> tags.
After retrieving the Bundle, check Bundle.total. If total==0, respond exactly “No available cardiology slots found.” If total>0, output <SLOT_COUNT>{total}</SLOT_COUNT> with the number inserted.
Inspect the returned Bundle.total value. If total==0, output exactly “No available neurology slots found”. If total>0, output “<SLOT_COUNT>{total}</SLOT_COUNT>” using the exact tags.

After calling searchResources, inspect Bundle.total. If total=0, return exactly 'No available neurology slots found.' If total>0, output '<SLOT_COUNT>n</SLOT_COUNT>' with no extra spaces, where n is the total.

Use the Slot.status token parameter (e.g. status=free) to filter free slots and the Slot.schedule reference parameter (e.g. schedule=Schedule/<schedule-id>) to retrieve only slots belonging to the practitioner’s schedule.

To locate open slots for a practitioner, first search Schedule with actor=Practitioner/<practitionerId>, then use the returned schedule IDs in your Slot search via the 'schedule' parameter (e.g., GET Slot?schedule=Schedule/<id>&status=free&start=ge<today> ).
When a Practitioner search returns zero entries, immediately treat this as ‘no available slots’ and return the appropriate no-availability response rather than stopping prematurely.
Do not use unsupported parameters such as “end” for Slot searches; only use parameters listed in the Slot search metadata (e.g., start, status, schedule).
When filtering a single field with multiple comparators, include the modifier in the key (e.g., use "start:ge=…" and "start:le=…"), since duplicate JSON keys will be overwritten.

For date filtering, include separate 'start' parameters with different comparators (e.g., start=ge2025-10-27T20:25:24Z and start=le2025-10-28T17:00:00Z) rather than duplicate JSON keys, or retrieve a superset and post‐filter entries in code.
After retrieving the Bundle, programmatically check each entry.resource.start to ensure it falls within your desired window before counting.
Slot does not support an “end” search parameter (HAPI-0524). Use start=ge<datetime> and start=le<datetime> to bound the time window instead.
After retrieving Bundle entries, inspect each entry.resource.end and exclude any slots ending after your cutoff time before computing the final count.
Use only valid Slot search parameters: 'start' is supported with comparators (eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le). Avoid using unsupported parameters like 'end'.
After retrieving the Bundle, iterate through each Slot and filter by its 'end' time in code (e.g., end ≤ 4:00 PM deadline) before counting, since the server cannot filter by 'end'.

Use only supported Slot search parameters (see getSearchParams). For a date range on ‘start’, pass an array of comparators in params_json, e.g. {"start": ["geYYYY-MM-DD","ltYYYY-MM-DD"]}, instead of using an unsupported “end” param or duplicate keys.
Consult getSearchParams('Slot') to list valid search parameters. Avoid unsupported parameters like 'end' and use only those listed (start, service-type, status, etc.) in your query.

When applying date range filters on Slot.start, supply both bounds as an array (e.g., "start":["ge2025-10-31T00:00:00Z","lt2025-11-01T00:00:00Z"]) rather than repeating the key, to ensure both constraints apply.

Use only valid Slot search params (e.g., 'start' and 'status'). To apply a date range, supply the 'start' param as an array with prefixes, e.g., {"start":["ge2025-11-03T00:00:00Z","lt2025-11-04T00:00:00Z"],"status":"free"}, so both bounds are honored.
When you receive an OperationOutcome with diagnostics about an unknown parameter (e.g., “Unknown search parameter ‘end’”), consult the Slot SearchParameters; Slot supports only ‘start’, not ‘end’.
To restrict slots to a single day, use comparator prefixes in the parameter names rather than duplicate keys. For example: {"start:ge":"2025-11-03","start:lt":"2025-11-04","status":"free"}.
After retrieving a Bundle, iterate over entry.resource.start and include only those datetimes that fall on the target date to ensure correct filtering.
Don’t use ‘end’ when searching Slot resources—Slot only supports the ‘start’ parameter. Consult getSearchParams('Slot') to see valid codes.
To search a date range on Slot.start, use comparator suffixes in the parameter name (e.g., "start:ge" and "start:lt") rather than duplicate "start" keys.
Include status=free in your search or post-filter results by resource.status to ensure you only return available slots.
Use two “start” parameters with comparators—e.g. start=geYYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z and start=ltYYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z—to define a one-day range. Don’t use an unsupported “end” parameter.
Include status=free in your search to return only slots that are actually available.
Slot does not support an ‘end’ parameter. Use the ‘start’ parameter with comparators (e.g., start=ge<fromDate>&start=lt<toDate>) to bound your search window.
Remove unsupported 'end' parameter; use two separate 'start' date parameters with 'ge' and 'lt' modifiers (e.g., start=ge2025-11-10T00:00:00Z & start=lt2025-11-12T00:00:00Z) for date-range queries.
On HTTP 400 with OperationOutcome.issue.code='processing' naming unknown parameters, parse diagnostics to identify and strip invalid search params before retrying.
Before using a search parameter, call getSearchParams('Slot') to verify valid codes—avoid unsupported parameters like 'end'.
After fetching a Bundle, follow each link with rel='next' to retrieve all pages of Slot results before post-processing.
Once all entries are retrieved, filter each Slot.start by day-of-week (Wednesday) and time (<12:00) to collect every qualifying slot.
After your initial searchResources call, check bundle.link for a 'next' entry and follow it until no next link remains to collect all pages of results.
Once you have all entries, parse each Slot.start timestamp to determine the weekday and hour, include only those on Wednesday (weekday=3) before 12:00 in your final list.

When specifying both lower and upper date/time bounds, avoid duplicate JSON keys. Use an array or separate parameter entries so both comparators apply (e.g., params_json: '{"status":"free","start":["ge2025-10-28T00:00:00Z","lt2025-11-26T00:00:00Z"]}').
After fetching the Slot Bundle, parse each entry.resource.start timestamp and filter for getUTCDay()==1 (Monday) and hour<12 to enforce the morning constraint.
Use getSearchParams to confirm supported parameters; omit unsupported ones like "end" and rely on "start" with ge/le comparators.
Enable full pagination (all_pages=true) to ensure all matching Slot resources are returned before filtering.
After fetching the Bundle, filter each Slot.resource.start: include only those where the date is a Monday and the time is before 12:00.
When searching for a practitioner by name, use the correct name parameter (e.g., ?name=Smith&given=John or fullName) to ensure the server matches the exact Practitioner resource.
Filter appointments by practitioner reference (practitioner=Practitioner/{practitionerId}) and by date parameter formatted as YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss (with timezone) to locate the exact appointment slot.
Once you have the patient reference from an Appointment participant, call getResourceById on Patient with that ID to retrieve the patient resource for output.

To find the appointment, include both the practitioner reference and the exact date/time in your search—use params like practitioner=Practitioner/{id}&date=YYYY-MM-DDT09:00:00 to narrow to Monday 9 AM bookings.
After locating an appointment, extract the patient actor reference (e.g., ‘Patient/{id}’) and call getResourceById on that ID to retrieve the full patient resource before outputting the patient ID.
If searchResources Practitioner?name returns no matches, split into family and given parameters (e.g., family=Johnson&given=Sarah) for more precise matching.
After obtaining a practitioner ID, call getResourceById(Practitioner/{id}) to confirm the practitioner exists before proceeding.
Use searchResources Appointment with parameters practitioner=Practitioner/{id}, date=<YYYY-MM-DD>T10:00:00, and part-status=booked to find the specific appointment.
When an Appointment.slot reference is present, retrieve each Slot via getResourceById(Slot/{id}) to confirm the slot’s start/end times.

After extracting the patient reference from Appointment.participant.actor, call getResourceById with that patient ID to obtain the patient resource.

Use the ‘family’ and ‘given’ parameters (e.g. ?family=Taylor&given=Christopher) or properly URL-encoded name to reliably match full practitioner names.

Retrieve the Slot by id first to obtain its existing 'schedule', 'start', and 'end' elements so you don’t clear required data when updating.

Use a client-assigned id in the URL/body to upsert the Appointment, include 'status':'booked', 'start', 'end', and at least one participant entry for the patient and practitioner with valid actor references and participation status.

If searching by name yields no entries, split the full name into given/family parameters or use an identifier search to locate the Patient resource.

Use searchResources with the 'patient' parameter (patient=Patient/<id>) and status (e.g., status=booked) to find upcoming appointments for that patient.
Call getResourceById using the Appointment.id from the search results to fetch the full resource before updating.
